title: Resilience review and mitigation plan for staged model deployment failure
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Summary: During a staged deployment on 2025-02-17 we observed a divergence between canary and production traffic for a recent model variant. Shadow traffic signals indicated degraded relevance on a subset of queries; the canary partially masked regressions due to insufficient sampling and metric sensitivity. Auto-rollback did not trigger because the configured thresholds were tuned for latency spikes, not semantic drift. Impact: A small percentage of production requests received lower-quality responses for ~45 minutes before we initiated a manual rollback. Root cause hypotheses: 1) Canary sampling window (2m) was too small relative to the slow-moving distribution shift; 2) Observability gaps: no weighted divergence metric combining relevance and hallucination proxies; 3) Shadow traffic fidelity mismatch: synthetic traffic in shadow used canonical prompts, not the long-tail prompts that revealed the regression; 4) Auto-rollback hysteresis and thresholds only monitored token-level latency/error rates, not NLU quality signals. Immediate containment steps taken: - Manual rollback to prior model at 2025-02-17T17:22 UTC - Re-enabled expanded shadow logging and captured representative payloads - Short-lived throttling of canary traffic to 2% until additional checks were implemented Lessons learned (high-level): - Canary policies must include semantic quality checks, not only latency/exception thresholds. - Shadow traffic must mirror production distribution; synthetic probes alone are insufficient. - Auto-rollback should support composite triggers (quality + latency + error) with tunable hysteresis. Proposed mitigation plan (this ticket): 1) Runbook updates: add a Canary Quality Checklist with concrete probes (BLEU-like relevance proxies, embedding divergence score, hallucination heuristics) and escalation paths. 2) Sentinel probes: add periodic long-tail prompt set (managed by Product & Solutions) to canary and shadow traffic to surface regressions. 3) Instrumentation: create a "shadow divergence score" (0-100) derived from embedding cosine drift + function-calling failure rate + hallucination classifier signal; expose as a primary canary metric. 4) Auto-rollback enhancements: support multi-signal thresholds, weighted aggregation, and a minimum evaluation window based on sample variance rather than fixed time. 5) Rollout policy changes: implement phased canary expansion with mandatory hold points and synthetic + shadow checks passing before each phase. 6) Test harness: add a simulated rollout test in CI that injects synthetic drift and validates that the auto-rollback triggers within expected bounds. 7) Dashboards/alerts: add a dedicated "Model Confidence" dashboard and an alert runbook mapping alert severities to rollback vs. human review actions. Acceptance criteria: - New canary checklist exists in the runbook and is used in at least 2 subsequent rollouts. - Shadow divergence score implemented and instrumented in console per-model metrics. - Auto-rollback accepts composite thresholds and triggers in simulated tests. - Synthetic long-tail probe set curated and accepted by Product. - Post-change rollout (staged by 2%) completes without semantic regression for 48 hours. Success metrics: reduction in undetected semantic regressions during rollouts by >80% (measured against prior incident baseline), rollback trigger time under 10 minutes in simulated regressions, and reduced manual rollback interventions by 90%.
